title: Transfer clipboard: concise shift transfer notes
content:
Quick context:
- Night shift (Leo) handed off after 03:20 UTC. Quiet baseline then a recurring spike in api-service 5xxs starting ~01:10 UTC; root cause looks related to Redis connection churn on cache keys with TTLs.
- Current status: degraded but functional; bulk of user traffic served from fallback cache layer, p95 latency ~420ms (target 300ms). No active pages open (alerts silenced briefly while stabilizing).

Incidents / items to watch (short):
1) Redis conn flapping (primary -> replica failover noise)
   - Symptom: `ERR max number of clients reached` + intermittent timeouts in app logs.
   - Mitigation applied last night: temporary connection pooling increase (env var REDIS_MAX_CONN=150) and turned on app-level circuit breaker for feature X.
   - TODO: coordinate with infra to check instance OS limits and redis maxclients. Ticket INFRA-1423 created (owner: Samir).
   - Quick check commands:
       kubectl -n prod logs deploy/api-service | grep -i "redis.*ERR" -n | tail -n 50
       redis-cli -h redis.primary.prod INFO clients | grep connected_clients
       ssh infra@bastion 'sudo ss -s | grep -i estab'  # quick network socket health check

2) Scheduled batch job (recommendation)
   - Daily embedding refresh runs at 02:00 UTC; might add load. Last run peaked 02:05-02:12. Consider rescheduling to stagger with morning traffic.

Short runbook snippets (for immediate triage):
- If API 5xx rate > 2% for > 5m:
    1) Check svc latency + errors dashboard (Dash: /d/svc-errors/api-service).
    2) Run: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=api-service -o wide` -> if >30% pods NotReady, escalate to SRE paging.
    3) If errors point to redis timeouts, flip feature flag `use_fallback_cache` to true: `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://admin.api/flags/use_fallback_cache/on`
    4) If still bad, roll previous deploy: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/api-service` (note: coordinate in #oncall).

- Restart steps for a single bad pod (use when logs indicate OOM or stuck threads):
    kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/api-service --selector=pod=NAME
    # or to delete specific pod: kubectl -n prod delete pod api-service-xxxxx --grace-period=30

Debugging snippets (copy/paste friendly):
- PromQL to gauge redis timeouts: `sum by(job) (increase(redis_server_command_duration_seconds_count{job="redis"}[5m]))`
- Count of api 5xxs last 15m: `increase(http_server_requests_total{job="api-service",status=~"5.."}[15m])`
- Find recent error trace ids in logs: `rg "trace_id" /var/log/api/*.log | tail -n 50`

Contacts / escalation matrix (fast):
- First oncall (this rotation): Asha Patel (me) - slack @asha, phone +1-555-0112 (use only for P1)
- Secondary: Leo Martinez - slack @leo, phone +1-555-0199
- SRE lead: Samir Bose - slack @samir, escalate if infra-level (redis cluster, networking)
- Database: Priya Kapoor (DB team) - slack @priya

Notes to incoming shift (things I did):
- Increased REDIS_MAX_CONN to 150 in k8s secret `redis-connections` at 02:50 UTC (short-term).
- Enabled `use_fallback_cache=true` for api-service to reduce pressure on redis at 03:04 UTC.
- Created INFRA-1423, attached logs + grafana graphs, assigned to Samir.
- Left a sticky comment on the PR that rolled deployment (github.com/redwood/repo/pull/332) indicating to monitor for subtle cachekey changes.

Unresolved / follow-ups:
- Confirm redis maxclients and ulimit on redis hosts. (Samir)
- Investigate why reconnection bursts coincide with the embedding refresh job; consider randomized jitter on job start. (OWNER: infra/ops)
- Add synthetic test hitting redis hot keys to recreate locally. (DEV-DEBUG)

Temporary knobs (what I changed and how to revert):
- REDIS_MAX_CONN now 150 in secret `redis-connections` -> revert: set back to 100 and restart deployment when infra confirms host limits.
- feature flag `use_fallback_cache` turned ON -> revert via admin endpoint or Admin UI.

Open questions / quick TODOs for you:
- Do we want to keep fallback cache on during business hours tomorrow morning? My vote: keep until infra confirms server-side limits.
- If we see >3% 5xxs after morning, escalate to incident channel and consider a short rollback window.

Scratch reminders (personal):
- add small script to run health checks automatically and notify #oncall when redis connected_clients > 120.
- write a short doc on safe rollout toggles for cache-related features.

If you need to take over now: ping @samir in #infra, run the `redis-cli INFO clients` check, then either raise the curtain to DB team or flip the fallback cache depending on severity.

Last 10 lines of relevant logs snapshot I copied:
"2026-03-12T02:53:12Z api-service ERROR redis: ERR max number of clients reached
2026-03-12T02:53:12Z api-service WARN request_id=abc123 trace_id=tr-789 latency=12ms status=500
2026-03-12T02:54:03Z api-service INFO fallback_cache used=true key=usr:cache:123
...
"

— end of transfer-clipboard quick note. Keep concise; leave me a slack note if you want details.
